title: OrionPay QBR - reliability + security controls
next_steps: Redwood to provide written confirmation of no prompt/response persistence and list of retained metadata
OrionPay to confirm whether Dedicated vs Private is required for their compliance posture
Schedule follow-up on audit logging and break-glass access
transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-03-11
Time: 10:30am PT
Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Naomi Feldman (Redwood CSM), Soojin Lee (Redwood Security), Elena Korsakov (OrionPay), Matt Reyes (OrionPay), Sanjay Gupta (OrionPay)

Topics (auto)
- QBR metrics and incidents
- Audit logs and access controls
- Retention / privacy requirements

Transcript
[00:18] Naomi Feldman: Thanks for joining. Well do the usual QBR: uptime, latency trends, then any upcoming security needs.
[03:02] Elena Korsakov: Overall things look stable. Were planning to expand to another workload, but security wants the privacy story really tight.
[03:18] Matt Reyes: Yeah. Specifically, we need assurance Redwood does not persist content. Not we dont train — I mean we dont want prompt/response stored anywhere, even briefly.
[03:44] Soojin Lee: Understood. We can support a configuration where prompt/response bodies are not written to logs/traces/support views. We still keep operational metadata for billing and availability.
[04:11] Matt Reyes: Thats the requirement. We call it zero data storage. We can allow request IDs, timestamps, status, and aggregated token counts.
[05:06] Sanjay Gupta: For debugging, does your team ever ask to turn on payload logging?
[05:14] Naomi Feldman: Not without explicit customer approval. We can also set policy so its disabled and requires an exception process.
[06:02] Matt Reyes: Well need that written.

[48:30] Naomi Feldman: Recap: OrionPay wants no prompt/response retention at rest. Redwood to send a written confirmation and outline metadata retained + the break-glass process.
